summary: Backend-only verification of CVLN Financial Core hardening (Mission P0.1). Created pytest suite (/app/backend/tests/) with 15 tests covering the API idempotency engine on POST /api/actions/send and POST /api/withdrawals (replay, conflict, per-user key scoping, failure retry), ledger double-entry integrity (/api/admin/ledger/integrity), /api/admin/financial-health, admin-only protection and non-regression of key-less send + coffre move. 12/15 passed. Idempotency replay protection works correctly (no double debit, same tx_id/wd_id returned, single ledger entry + single transaction persisted); 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT returned for same key + different body on both endpoints; ledger is balanced (per_asset_sum JCC == 0) and cache_mismatches == [] ; admin endpoints return 403 for non-admin and 401 unauthenticated. Two real defects found: (1) an Idempotency-Key used on a request that fails validation is permanently poisoned (record stays PROCESSING -> every retry returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS); (2) jcc_supply_reconciled=false / severity=CRITICAL caused by legacy non-ledger data in the DB (orphan coffres worth 173,400 JCC + a stale 100 JCC entry for deleted user acct_cash_u_idem). Proved by a delta test that the discrepancy is NOT changed by ledger operations (delta = 0), i.e. the ledger code is consistent but legacy data was never backfilled.

critical.issue: idem_begin() inserts the idempotency_records doc with state=PROCESSING BEFORE business validation. If the request then fails (e.g. 400 'Solde insuffisant') or the process crashes, the record is never finished/removed, so the same key+body can never be retried: it returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS forever (verified: 400 then 409). Fix: wrap the handler so failures mark the record FAILED/delete it, and add a TTL index on created_at to auto-expire stuck PROCESSING records.

jcc_supply_reconciled=false and severity=CRITICAL on the current dataset. Root cause is legacy data, not the ledger code: 4 orphan coffres of user_b02e5638bc1a (user no longer exists) hold 173,400 JCC in coffres.amount_cc with no ledger entries, plus a stale ledger entry crediting acct_sys_clearing +100 for the deleted test user acct_cash_u_idem. Fix: one-off migration to post legacy coffre/user balances into the ledger (issuance -> account) or purge orphan coffres/stale entries, otherwise the health endpoint permanently reports CRITICAL.

minor.issue: Cache-vs-derived check is limited to .limit(50) users and ignores coffres.amount_cc vs acct_coffre_* derived balances, so coffre cache drift (the exact source of the current supply mismatch) is invisible in cache_mismatches.
No IBAN format validation (any string accepted) in WithdrawRequest.
Updates coffres.amount_cc / users.balance_cc BEFORE ledger_post and creates a 0-amount transaction; no Idempotency-Key support, so a duplicated client call moves funds twice.

action_items: Release/expire idempotency records on failure (mark FAILED or delete) + TTL index, so failed requests are retryable with the same key
Backfill or purge legacy non-ledger balances (orphan coffres of user_b02e5638bc1a = 173,400 JCC, stale acct_cash_u_idem entry) so financial-health reports reconciled/INFO
Extend integrity check to coffre accounts and remove the 50-user limit (paginate)
Add Idempotency-Key support to /api/coffres/{id}/move (value movement without replay protection)
critical_code_review_comments: server.py send_money/create_withdrawal: idem_begin before validation creates poisoned keys; move record creation after validation or add failure cleanup in a try/except.

add_transaction() is called without idempotency_key from send/withdrawal, so replay safety depends solely on the API layer; pass a deterministic key (e.g. idem_id) into ledger_post for defence in depth.
server.py is 1169 lines - split into routers (auth, wallet, ledger, admin, agents, card).
get_or_seed_card(): duplicated db.cards.find_one call (lines 211-212), dead code.

ledger_integrity()/financial_health() duplicate the same per-asset aggregation loop in Python; extract a shared helper and use a Mongo aggregation instead of a per-entry Python loop (O(n) round-trip cost).
seed_data_creation: Seeded via pymongo: TEST_ta_admin_* (is_admin=true, 1000 JCC) and TEST_ta_user_* (500 JCC), each funded with a BALANCED ledger entry (issuance -> acct_cash_<uid>) plus user_sessions token. All test users, sessions, transactions, withdrawals, coffres, idempotency records and ledger entries were deleted at teardown (verified: 0 TEST_* docs remain, ledger back to 1 pre-existing entry).
test_credentials: /app/memory/test_credentials.md is an empty template (no credentials). Auth is Emergent Google; tests seed users+sessions directly in MongoDB (see conftest._mk_user).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -n 0 -v (use -n 0 to avoid xdist cross-class races on shared balances). conftest.py seeds users/sessions with ledger-consistent funding and cleans up. The 3 known failures are: test_failed_request_key_is_not_poisoned (idempotency poison bug), test_financial_health + test_supply_discrepancy_unchanged_by_ledger_ops (legacy 173,500 JCC non-ledger data). The 'unchanged by ledger ops' half of that test already passes (delta 0), so once legacy data is backfilled/purged both should go green. Frontend was intentionally not tested.
rca_of_the_issue: 1) Poisoned idempotency key: idem_begin() inserts state=PROCESSING before amount/balance validation in send_money and create_withdrawal, and idem_finish() only runs on success; HTTPException paths leave the record PROCESSING, and the unique idem_id index then makes every retry raise 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. 2) Supply mismatch: financial_health computes circulation = sum(users.balance_cc) + sum(coffres.amount_cc) and compares with -sum(system accounts). The DB contains 4 coffres (173,400 JCC) belonging to a deleted user that were seeded directly into amount_cc without any ledger entry, plus one stale ledger entry (+100 to acct_sys_clearing) whose user cash account no longer maps to an existing user, so the comparison is off by 173,500 JCC regardless of new operations.
